title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (2026)
summary: How to request medical records from Memorial Sloan Kettering in 2026: current forms, contact details, the Requester Portal, MyChart, HIPAA and New York rules.
body_markdown:
Requesting medical records from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSK) works differently depending on whether the requester is the patient or an authorized third party like a law firm, and timing depends on the request method, the records requested, and whether the paperwork is complete. For personal injury attorneys handling cases involving cancer diagnoses or treatment complications, delays can stall settlement negotiations and frustrate clients.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-powered medical record retrieval with automated follow-up and authorization validation before submission, and reports an average turnaround of a couple of weeks for complete records. Individual MSK requests may vary.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


MSK's Release of Information office can be reached by phone (646-227-2089), fax (212-557-0531 or 646-227-3545), or email (HIMROI@mskcc.org). The authorization form lists the Health Information Management Department at 633 Third Avenue, 11th Floor, New York, NY 10017.


-


MSK's current authorization form asks for patient identification, recipient details, record categories, purpose and expiration, and a patient or personal representative signature, with specific boxes for HIV-related and genetic information.


-


Authorized third-party organizations, including law firms, can now use MSK's Release of Information Requester Portal to submit, track, pay for, and download record requests.


-


HIPAA generally requires covered entities to act on qualifying patient access requests within[30 calendar days](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/how-timely-must-a-covered-entity-be/index.html) , with one extension of up to 30 days when notice requirements are met.


-


Records from 2020 onward can be viewed in MSK MyChart, and MSK says formal copies requested through MyChart are usually available in 1 or 2 business days.


-


Codes Health validates authorizations before submission and verifies completeness before delivery, which helps avoid the rejections and gaps that slow MSK retrieval.


## **Understanding the Memorial Sloan Kettering Medical Records Request Process**


### **Why You Might Need Your Medical Records from MSK**


Medical records from Memorial Sloan Kettering serve critical functions in legal proceedings. Personal injury attorneys need comprehensive treatment documentation to establish damages, identify pre-existing conditions, and document future medical needs. Cancer treatment records are particularly complex because they span multiple specialties, including oncology consultations, surgical reports, radiology imaging, pathology findings, and chemotherapy protocols.


For mass tort litigation involving toxic exposure or pharmaceutical injuries, MSK records may contain evidence relevant to causation analysis, including diagnosis history, clinical findings, and documented exposure history. Whether they establish legal or medical causation usually depends on expert analysis.


### **Overview of the Request Lifecycle**


A typical third-party request means getting the right authorization or proof of authority, submitting it through one of MSK's channels, following up after the recommended wait, and verifying completeness on arrival.


For standard Release of Information requests, MSK asks requesters to[wait 10 business days](https://www.mskcc.org/experience/become-patient/how-to-get-your-medical-records-at-msk) before asking for a status update. That's a follow-up instruction, not a guaranteed or minimum processing time.


## **Required Forms for Memorial Sloan Kettering Medical Records Release**


### **Finding the Correct MSK Authorization Forms**


MSK publishes an[Authorization and Request form](https://www.mskcc.org/teaser/release-information-medical-records-form.pdf) for release of medical records. HIPAA's requirements for a valid authorization are set out in[45 CFR § 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.508) . Complete all fields that apply to your request, and give MSK enough information to identify the patient, the records requested, the authorized recipient, and the authority for disclosure.


### **Key Sections to Complete on the Release Form**


MSK's current two-page form includes:


-


**Patient identification** : Name, date of birth, and Medical Record Number (MRN) if known


-


**Request type** : Including "Attorney"


-


**Recipient information** : Name, address, phone, and fax for record delivery


-


**Record types requested** : Checkboxes for Labs, Pathology, Radiology, Operative Reports, Discharge Summary, Consultation Reports, HIV-related information, Genetic information, Medical Abstract, or Other


-


**Purpose of disclosure** : The form states "At the request of the individual"


-


**Expiration** : The form states an expiration of one year from the date signed


-


**Signature and date** : From the patient or personal representative, with representative details where applicable


The form has no date-range field, "legal proceedings" purpose option, or separate mental health or substance use checkboxes, and doesn't require an original wet signature.


### **Specific Authorizations for Family Access and Sensitive Records**


When requesting records on behalf of someone else, the documentation required depends on the requester's authority. For a deceased patient, New York law recognizes several possible qualified persons. When no personal representative has been appointed, for example, a distributee may have access rights with the required statutory documentation, so an executor or probate court order isn't always required. For minor patients, parents and guardians may have access rights, but[New York law](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/PBH/18) can limit them depending on the treatment involved and other circumstances.


MSK's form includes explicit boxes for HIV-related and genetic information, and those should be checked when that information is needed. Mental health and substance use records can carry separate legal requirements, so confirm with MSK whether additional authorization is needed for other specially protected records.


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can lead to rejection, requests for correction, and added delay. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


## **Contact Information and Submission Methods for MSK Medical Records**


### **Direct Contact Details for Memorial Sloan Kettering**


MSK's current[records contact information](https://www.mskcc.org/experience/become-patient/how-to-get-your-medical-records-at-msk) includes:


-


**Phone** : 646-227-2089 (Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern Time)


-


**Email** : HIMROI@mskcc.org


-


**Fax** : 212-557-0531 or 646-227-3545


-


**HIM address listed on the authorization form** : Health Information Management Department, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, 633 Third Avenue, 11th Floor, New York, NY 10017


Because procedures can change, confirm current instructions before sending a new request.


### **Submission Methods for Law Firms**


-


**Requester Portal** : MSK now operates a Release of Information[Requester Portal](https://www.mskcc.org/privacy/requestor-portal-terms-of-use-and-end-user-license-agreement) for authorized third-party organizations, including law firms. Authorized users can submit, manage, track, pay for, receive, and download record requests, and MSK may ask for supporting documentation establishing authority.


-


**Email and fax** : Both remain available. For email, attach the completed authorization as a PDF and use a subject line with the patient's last name and date of birth. For fax, use a cover sheet marked "ATTN: Health Information Management Department" with your callback number.


-


**Phone and mail** : Phone works best for follow-up and doesn't replace a written authorization. Mail goes to the HIM address on the form.


### **Following Up on Your Request**


After 10 business days, call 646-227-2089 with the patient name, date of birth, and submission date, and log the update in your case file.


If MSK asks for corrections or more information, document what you sent and confirm the request's current status rather than assuming a fixed timeline has restarted.


## **Accessing Your Memorial Sloan Kettering Medical Records Online**


### **Steps to Create a MyMSK Account**


Patients can register for[MSK MyChart](https://www.mskcc.org/experience/become-patient/how-to-get-your-medical-records-at-msk) or ask their care team for registration help. Records from 2020 onward can be viewed in MyChart, and patients can request a formal copy from any year through Sharing Hub.


MyChart is a patient portal, so attorneys don't use it directly. Clients with active accounts can download and share their records, which can speed things up for recent treatment. For firm-initiated requests, the third-party Requester Portal is the relevant channel.


### **What Information is Available Through the Patient Portal**


The 21st Century Cures Act's[information-blocking rules](https://healthit.gov/information-blocking/) promote timely access to electronic health information and prohibit certain practices that interfere with access, subject to exceptions. Through MSK MyChart, patients can use:


-


**My Record** to view information such as test results, visits, medications, and forms


-


**Sharing Hub** to request a formal copy of their medical record


MSK says[formal copies requested](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/patient-education/21st-century-cures-act) through MyChart are usually available in the Documents Center within 1 or 2 business days.


### **Limitations of Online Access**


MyChart shouldn't be treated as the complete litigation record. MSK's[portal terms](https://mskmychart.mskcc.org/MyChart/Authentication/Login/StandardFile?option=TermsAndConditions) explain that some portions of the medical record may not be technically available through the portal, and documentation such as complete billing records or pathology slides may need separate requests.


For comprehensive retrieval across multiple treatment periods and document types, a formal request is still necessary. Codes Health retrieves records through claims clearinghouses, custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone to pursue complete documentation regardless of when treatment occurred.


## **Ensuring Completeness: What to Look for in Your MSK Records**


### **Key Sections to Verify in Retrieved Records**


When records arrive, verify them against your original request:


-


**Patient identification** : Confirm name, date of birth, and MRN match your client


-


**Treatment period coverage** : Confirm the relevant treatment period is represented


-


**Record type completeness** : Verify that all checked categories (Labs, Pathology, Radiology, and so on) are present


-


**Legibility** : Make sure all pages are readable and not cut off during scanning


-


**Billing documentation** : Confirm billing statements are included if requested


### **Addressing Missing Information or Discrepancies**


Common gaps can include radiology images, which have a dedicated workflow through MyChart and MSK's Radiology Film Library; pathology slides, which may need specific requests; billing records requested separately from clinical documentation; and outside records the patient brought to MSK that originated elsewhere.


If records look incomplete, contact the Release of Information office or use the applicable requester workflow to identify what's missing. Be specific about date ranges, record types, or treatment locations.

Codes Health's completeness verification checks delivered records against the original request before closing the retrieval. When records appear incomplete, the service works with MSK to resolve the gaps before returning the completed set to your firm.

## **Navigating HIPAA and New York Rules for MSK Records**


### **Patient Rights Under HIPAA**


The HIPAA Privacy Rule gives patients the right to request copies of their records, request amendments to inaccurate information, and receive an accounting of certain disclosures. For qualifying right-of-access requests, a covered entity generally must act within 30 calendar days, with one extension of up to 30 days if it gives the required written notice within the initial period.


That timeline applies to the patient's HIPAA right of access. Attorney requests can take different legal paths, such as a patient access request, a patient-directed request, an authorization-based disclosure, or a legal-process request, and the timing and fee rules can differ for each.


### **New York Public Health Law § 18**


New York Public Health Law § 18 adds patient-access protections. For qualifying requests, it generally requires an opportunity to inspect records within 10 days and requires copies within a reasonable time. Separately, MSK's[patient rights statement](https://www.mskcc.org/experience/become-patient/patients-rights) says patients may obtain a copy for a reasonable fee within 30 days after a written request to Health Information Management.


Under § 18, an attorney counts as a "qualified person" when holding a power of attorney explicitly authorizing a written records request, which isn't the same thing as a routine HIPAA authorization.


### **Ensuring Secure Transmission of Records**


MSK offers electronic delivery options and secure portal workflows. Firms using the Requester Portal are responsible for protecting their credentials and the records after download. Your firm should also use encrypted storage and access controls.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it typically take to get medical records from Memorial Sloan Kettering?**


There's no single MSK processing time for every request. For patients requesting formal records through MyChart, MSK says records are usually available within 1 or 2 business days. For other Release of Information requests, MSK asks requesters to wait at least 10 business days before asking for a status update. HIPAA's patient-access rule generally requires action within 30 calendar days, with one permitted extension. Codes Health reports an average turnaround of a couple of weeks for complete records across its retrieval service, and individual MSK requests may vary.


### **Can I request my child's medical records from MSK?**


Parents and legal guardians may have authority to access a minor's records, but that authority isn't unlimited. New York law protects certain confidential treatment and permits restrictions in specified circumstances, and MSK applies age-specific privacy controls for adolescent portal access. Contact MSK if you're unsure which authorization or proof of authority is needed.


### **What if I find an error in my Memorial Sloan Kettering medical records?**


HIPAA lets patients request amendments to information in a designated record set. Submit a written request to MSK's Health Information Management Department identifying the information you believe is incorrect and why. A covered entity generally has 60 days to act, with one permitted extension.


### **Is there a fee for requesting medical records from MSK?**


MSK states that patients may obtain copies for a reasonable fee. Under New York Public Health Law § 18, charges to qualified persons can't exceed the provider's costs, paper copies are capped at $0.75 per page, and access can't be denied solely for inability to pay. HIPAA applies separate cost-based fee rules to patient access requests, and following[Ciox Health v. Azar](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/court-order-right-of-access/index.html) , those patient-rate limits don't generally apply to records sent to a third party under an authorization. Confirm the applicable charge with MSK before submitting a high-volume request.


### **Can a lawyer request medical records directly from Memorial Sloan Kettering?**


Yes, when the lawyer or firm has adequate legal authority. MSK's Requester Portal serves authorized third-party organizations, including law firms, and may require a signed authorization or other supporting documentation. Records can also be disclosed through other lawful processes: a court order, or a[subpoena or discovery request](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/what-satisfactory-assurances-must-a-covered-entity-receive-before-it-responds-to-a-subpoena/index.html) that meets HIPAA's safeguards, such as satisfactory assurances of patient notice or a qualified protective order.
